items: Know Your True Numbers: List every fixed monthly expense including rent, utilities, insurance, minimum debt payments, groceries, and transportation with their exact dollar amounts rather than estimates or guesses.
Know Your True Numbers: Review your last three months of bank and credit card statements to calculate your actual variable spending on dining out, subscriptions, shopping, and entertainment.
Know Your True Numbers: Add your fixed expenses plus a realistic grocery and utility estimate plus fifteen percent for unexpected costs to determine your real survival number.
Know Your True Numbers: Subtract your survival number from your current monthly income to identify your financial gap and see exactly how much you need to cover each month.

Leave Without Guilt: Write a brief, professional resignation letter that expresses gratitude for the experience and provides a reasonable notice period instead of venting complaints or criticizing management.
Leave Without Guilt: Deliver your resignation in person to your direct manager if possible rather than through email or text message so you maintain control of the narrative and leave on good terms.
Leave Without Guilt: Document your ongoing projects, pending deadlines, and processes in a clear handover document so your team isn't stranded after you leave and you don't get dragged back in.
Leave Without Guilt: Collect personal contact information from trusted colleagues before leaving because you may need professional references, networking connections, or advice in the future.

Recover Before Returning: Structure your first weeks with intentional boundaries around sleep, meals, movement, and rest so your body actually recovers instead of just spinning without the pressure of work.
Recover Before Returning: Calculate how many months your savings will last at your survival spending rate so you can make decisions from a place of clarity instead of panic as time passes.
Recover Before Returning: Resist taking freelance or consulting work immediately because your body and mind need genuine rest, not just a different wrapper on the same exhausting pace.

Recover Before Returning: Before applying to anything, spend time reflecting on what type of work, environment, and boundaries you actually need so you don't just recreate the conditions that burned you out.
